title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption — Missing Rate Limiting
description: The sensitive endpoint '/identity/api/auth/signup' accepted 15 rapid requests without any rate limiting (no HTTP 429 responses). This enables brute-force attacks on credentials/OTPs and resource-exhaustion abuse.
poc_request:
POST /identity/api/auth/signup  x15 rapid requests
Observed status codes: [400]
poc_response: No 429 (Too Many Requests) returned across 15 requests.
remediation: Implement rate limiting on authentication and other sensitive endpoints (per-IP and per-account quotas, backoff, CAPTCHA after repeated failures). Return HTTP 429 when limits are exceeded.

title: Broken Authentication — JWT alg:none Accepted
description: The endpoint '/identity/api/v2/user/dashboard' rejected an invalid token but accepted a JWT with algorithm set to 'none' and no signature. The server does not verify token signatures, allowing an attacker to forge tokens and impersonate any user.
remediation: Reject tokens using the 'none' algorithm. Explicitly configure the JWT library to only accept the expected signing algorithm (e.g. RS256 or HS256) and always verify the signature.

title: BFLA — Admin Function Reachable by Regular User
description: A regular (non-admin) user reached the privileged endpoint '/workshop/api/management/users/all' and received HTTP 200. Function-level authorization appears to be missing or not enforced for this administrative function.
remediation: Enforce role-based access control on every administrative and privileged endpoint. Deny by default; require an explicit authorization check that the caller holds the necessary role before executing privileged functionality.

title: Vertical Privilege Escalation (role-aware)
description: A regular (non-admin) user successfully performed GET /workshop/api/management/users/all, which the admin account can also perform and which rejects unauthenticated requests (admin: HTTP 200, anonymous: HTTP 401, regular user: HTTP 200). The endpoint enforces authentication but not role-based authorization, allowing vertical privilege escalation.
poc_request:
GET /workshop/api/management/users/all
Authorization: <REGULAR_USER_TOKEN>
(admin can do this; anonymous is blocked; regular user should be blocked but is not)
remediation: Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) at the function level on the server. Verify the caller's role/permissions before executing privileged operations; return 403 Forbidden for users whose role does not permit the action. Do not rely on authentication alone or on the client hiding the endpoint.
